<h1 align="center">CASTAWAY</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>A ten-hour lo-fi video of one tiny island, one tall palm and no signal whatsoever.</b><br>
  <sub>Unofficial and drawn from scratch: inspired by <i>Johnny Castaway</i>, the 1992 desert-island screensaver. Not affiliated with it or its owners.</sub>
</p>

A young woman, a tall palm, a raft and a great deal of time. She idles, nodding to the music in her headphones, and every so often something happens: her message in a bottle drifts straight back to her, a drone delivers a parcel that turns out to be more headphones, a shark in headphones nods along on the beat, and a coconut lands on a hermit crab, who walks off wearing it. That is her phone in the picture, face up on the sand. It says *No network*. It is right. There is one bar, at the very top of the palm.

Sunny, hand-painted coastal anime, always daytime, 16:9 at 1080p, made for YouTube. **[More than 90 activities](activities.toml)** on four timers, from every few minutes to once every few hours, plus follow-ups that only ever happen after another one. Each starts on the next bar of the music, so the gags land on the beat. **Every sound is synthesized from code** by [`tools/make_audio.py`](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, no borrowed loops, no recordings.

```sh
python tools/serve.py
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

<p align="center">

</p>

The renderer is [a web page](web/index.html) with a live preview and an export button: frame-exact H.264 straight out of the browser, and the server mixes in the sound for a YouTube-ready MP4. Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm. It is in development, so no video is out yet. The phone has been told.

<details>
<summary><b>Menu 1 · Messages</b>: the inbox, which is mostly gags</summary>

```text
 INBOX                                         Nutwork: 1 bar (top of palm only)
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  From: you          Your message in a bottle. It drifted straight back.
  From: a bottle     A different one, much later. Somebody wrote back.
  From: a drone      Parcel delivered. Contents: another pair of headphones.
  From: a shark      He wears headphones. He nods on the beat. That's all.
  From: a turtle     Just visiting.
  From: a crate      A grey tabby with a white chest. Climbs the palm, naps,
                     and one day floats away again. Comes back another time.
  From: a tour boat  Selfies. Lots of selfies.
  From: the palm     A coconut fell on a hermit crab. The crab now wears it.
  From: the horizon  A ship went past. You were busy with a coconut.
  From: a hydrofoil  A wave, a shaka, and he carves off.
  From: you          Walked out over the water. Back with an iced coffee.
                     You could leave any time.
  From: the tide     Your sandcastle has been collected.
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Drafts             Fire by friction. A hammock. A lookout up the palm.
                     Spear fishing. A kumara, planted, growing all video.
  Sent               Waving for rescue. (See: From: the horizon.)
```

Meanwhile the scene keeps itself busy. Shore waves and drifting cloud shadows are built; distant birds, planes with vapour trails, whale pods, dolphins, sailboats, sandpipers, a gecko and a rain shower are planned. More than two dozen entries in all, none of them in a hurry.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Menu 2 · Calendar</b>: how ten hours fill up</summary>

```text
 CALENDAR                                      a typical 10-hour run, by timer
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  regular      every 2 to 5 min     about 155  ████████████████████████████████
  occasional   every 12 to 25 min   about 30   ██████
  rare         every 30 to 60 min   about 13   ███
  super rare   every 3 to 6 hours   about 2    ▌  (3 a run at most)
  chained      only after another   follow-ups
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  busy about a third of the time · idle the rest · every start waits for the
  next bar of the music, every 3 seconds
```

Lanes let things overlap: the cat, the turtle, the sea and sky, the shore and the kumara patch each have a lane of their own, and get on with their day while she gets on with hers. That is how a ship can sail past while she is busy with a coconut, and the ship has been known to wait until she is. The default run is 10:00:00 with seed 1992: same seed, same schedule. Typical counts are the median of 200 simulated runs, as the file's own header says, and [`python tools/schedule.py`](tools/schedule.py) checks the calendar and simulates a run for you.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Menu 3 · Tones</b>: every sound, synthesized</summary>

```text
 TONES
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Theme ............ a seamless 60-second loop: 80 BPM, F major, ii-V-I-vi,
                     20 bars of exactly 3 seconds
  Band ............. electric piano, kalimba lead, soft drums, vinyl crackle
  Ocean ............ also a seamless 60-second loop
  Loudness ......... -14 LUFS, true peak at or below -1 dBTP
  Volume ........... in master, and per routine
  Sound files ...... more than 150, every one written by tools/make_audio.py
  Samples used ..... 0. No borrowed loops, no recordings, no third-party
                     licences
  Listened to ...... not yet, by anyone
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

The phone's soft key says *Listen*. Nobody has pressed it. Its screen loop is 21 bars of 3 seconds, so its pages turn on the theme's bar lines too, in total silence. It is a picture.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Menu 4 · Settings</b>: the renderer and the tools</summary>

```sh
python tools/serve.py              # the renderer: live preview, MP4 export
                                   # then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
python tools/schedule.py           # check the schedule, simulate a 10-hour run
python tools/render_demo.py --dev  # a dev reel of every activity, with a HUD
```

[`tools/serve.py`](tools/serve.py) serves [the renderer](web/index.html), which exports frame-exact video in the browser (WebCodecs H.264; it measured 68 to 78 frames a second at 1080p in Chrome); the server then mixes the sound and joins the two into an MP4. [`tools/render_demo.py`](tools/render_demo.py) is the older Python reference renderer. Hard cuts and stepped movement are the motion defaults, and the phone screen agrees: it has never once faded. Always daytime, by rule. The project's log of decisions is [MUSING.md](MUSING.md).

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Menu 5 · Phone info</b>: credits, greetz, and what's on the sand</summary>

```text
 PHONE INFO
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Model ............ DRIFTCELL. Invented: it does not exist, and neither does
                     the network (Nutwork: 1 bar, top of the palm only)
  Screen ........... 84 x 48, two tones. The logo fits the 72 x 14 space with
                     a pixel to spare. All drawn for this README
  Battery .......... full. It has been on the idle screen for ten hours
  Inspired by ...... Johnny Castaway, the 1992 desert-island screensaver.
                     Unofficial: not affiliated with it or its owners
  Everything else .. drawn, coded and synthesized for this project
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  GREETZ   the Bottle Return Desk · the Palm Summit Alpine Club ·
           the Ringtone Abstinence League · everyone who meant to watch
           ten hours and watched four minutes
```

Look around the phone: the spare headphones from the drone, an iced coffee (she could leave any time), a kumara with its label, her footprints, and a hermit crab in his coconut, hopping about the beach a few pixels at a time. A palm frond's shadow sways over everything. The shore washing in at the corner and the cloud shadow drifting across are the two scene effects the video already has. The snake on the screen is not in the video. It is just passing through.

</details>
